title: Oakland and Berkeley Rent Increases for 2027: The New Numbers, and Which One Applies to Each Unit

findings.quote: In Berkeley it's January 1: tenancies that began in 2025 or earlier can take 2.5% on January 1, 2027, and tenancies that began in 2026 wait until January 1, 2028.
findings.root_cause: The quick answer, FAQ 3, script and several tables omit the fully-covered-unit qualifier and make first eligibility sound automatic. The body later acknowledges lease and compliance restrictions. The AGA changes the rent ceiling; banking may make an actual increase different from 2.5%. The FAQ's 'on or after' wording also extends a 2027 figure beyond its verified year. Verified against the Berkeley AGA page: https://rentboard.berkeleyca.gov/rights-responsibilities/rent-levels/annual-general-adjustment
findings.fix: Replace the quoted sentence with: 'For fully rent-controlled Berkeley units, 2025 move-ins first become AGA-eligible on January 1, 2027; 2026 move-ins first become eligible on January 1, 2028, subject to the lease, proper notice and Rent Board compliance. The 2027 AGA is 2.5%; eligible banked AGAs can affect the actual increase.' Replace 'on or after January 1, 2027' in FAQ 1 with 'during calendar year 2027'. Apply the fully-covered-unit and eligibility qualifiers to FAQ 3, the script, tables and companion page.
findings.future_prevention: Check coverage, eligibility, rent ceiling and actual increase separately; synchronize both scripts.

findings.quote: A banked increase can add more, up to three times the current rate (6.9%).
findings.root_cause: The wording can be read as allowing 6.9% of banking in addition to 2.3%. The limit applies to the total CPI-plus-banking increase. The FAQ is clearer but should be explicit. Source: https://www.oaklandca.gov/Community/Housing-Programs-Support/For-Landlords/Allowable-Rent-Increases/Learn-More-About-Allowable-Rent-Increases
findings.fix: Replace with: 'Eligible banked CPI amounts can be added, but the combined current CPI plus banking increase cannot exceed 6.9% this cycle.' Use that same total-limit wording in the Key Facts table and FAQ 4.
findings.future_prevention: Write every banking limit as a total or an additional amount explicitly.

findings.quote: Confirm the unit's last increase took effect at least 12 months earlier.
findings.root_cause: Oakland's action list omits registration compliance, the first-increase wait and the six-month RAP-notice prerequisite. Having a tax certificate also differs from attaching the required document. Verified on the City's allowable-increases page and rent-registration FAQs.
findings.fix: Replace with: 'Confirm the unit is registered with RAP, the first increase is at least 12 months after move-in, any prior increase was at least 12 months ago, and at least six months have passed since the tenant first received the RAP Notice.' Replace 'have a current Business Tax Certificate or a payment plan for delinquent business taxes' with 'attach a current Business Tax Certificate or, for a CPI-only increase, a current signed City payment plan for delinquent business taxes'. Retain the current-certificate requirement for banking. Add an internal link to the existing Oakland rent-control deep dive.
findings.future_prevention: Use a complete jurisdiction-specific eligibility checklist before calendar advice; source: https://www.oaklandca.gov/Community/Housing-Programs-Support/For-Landlords/Allowable-Rent-Increases/Learn-More-About-Allowable-Rent-Increases

findings.quote: Single-family homes and condos are exempt from AB 1482 only if the tenant received the required written exemption notice.
findings.root_cause: In an exemption summary, the notice-only description is incomplete: qualifying ownership also matters. A corporate owner cannot create this exemption just by delivering notice. Official DRE 2026 guide, printed p.39 (PDF p.45), summarizes the ownership and notice tests: https://www.dre.ca.gov/publications/ResourceGuidebook/2026_Landlord_Tenant_Guide.pdf
findings.fix: Replace with: 'The single-family-home/condo exemption also requires qualifying ownership: no REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, plus the required written exemption notice. Notice alone does not establish eligibility.' Cite Civil Code §1947.12(d)(5)(A)-(B), with the DRE guide as the accessible official corroboration.
findings.future_prevention: Check exemption conditions as a conjunction; never reduce an exemption to its notice requirement.

findings.quote: The same math works for any date: count back 30 days for personal service, or 35 if you mail the notice.
findings.root_cause: The blanket instruction excludes the 90-day branch and the mailing-origin distinction. The FAQ also omits the cumulative 12-month test. The published November 25/December 1 targets are conservative, not late; do not 'correct' them as invalid. Official DRE 2026 guide, printed pp.44-46: https://www.dre.ca.gov/publications/ResourceGuidebook/2026_Landlord_Tenant_Guide.pdf
findings.fix: Replace with: 'For an otherwise lawful increase, use at least 30 days when the cumulative increase is 10% or less over the preceding 12 months; use 90 days above 10%, measured from the lowest rent in that period. First-class mailing within California adds five days; mailing from elsewhere can require longer. November 25 and December 1 are conservative planning targets for a January 1 increase that qualifies for 30-day notice.' Apply these qualifications to the Key Facts notice rows, calendar, FAQ 5 and script. Add the official DRE guide to Sources.
findings.future_prevention: Test both notice branches and mailing origin; label conservative targets as planning targets.

findings.quote: The 2027 numbers are set: 2.5% in Berkeley, 2.3% in Oakland through July, and 8.8% under AB 1482 through July.

findings.fix: Use this scoped GBP draft for comparison: 'Planning a 2027 rent increase? Berkeley’s 2027 AGA is 2.5%; Oakland’s annual CPI allowance is 2.3% through July 31, 2027.
